title: apricity-link Session: join, allocation-free capture to a clock line, follow-only, peer events, ScriptedSession
description:
## Intent
The session API every Link user in Apricity goes through (play, serve, the harness, later the Swift app).

## Steps
1. `crates/apricity-link/src/lib.rs`: `Session` (join with a proposed tempo and quantum; peers; enable start/stop sync; leave). An audio-thread capture that returns M1's `ClockLine` for a given output time, allocation-free.
2. Follow-only by construction: no public method commits a tempo or a start/stop to the session. The only tempo Apricity ever proposes is its initial one, when there are no peers at join time.
3. Events for the control thread: peers changed, tempo changed, start/stop changed (for messages).
4. `ScriptedSession` (same trait): a timeline of tempo, start/stop and peer events on a virtual clock, for specs and unit tests.
5. Unit tests: the capture allocation count is zero; no tempo commit happens after join (spy on the binding); scripted events arrive in order.

## Verify
`cargo test -p apricity-link`.

Commit: `feat(<this task id>): Link session, follow-only`.

## Protocol
Specs first, watched red; log decisions, problems and outcomes with `kbs comment`; run Verify and paste the tail. Every Bash call starts `export PATH=$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH && cd /Users/home/Projects/Apricity`; cargo with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` under `safe-run.sh --`. Never change dependencies to make a build pass. Sub-agents never commit, push or close.
